html:
José Saramago was a Portuguese novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1998, the first writer in Portuguese to do so.

Born to a family of poor farm workers, he worked as a mechanic, civil servant and journalist, and became known as a novelist only in his late fifties. His novels, such as Baltasar and Blimunda and Blindness, use long sentences with little punctuation and mix history, fable and irony.

A lifelong communist and an atheist, he clashed with the Portuguese government over his Gospel According to Jesus Christ in 1992 and moved to the Spanish island of Lanzarote. His work brought Portuguese literature to a world audience, following Camões and Fernando Pessoa. See Portugal and the Nobel Prize in Literature.
sum: José Saramago was a Portuguese novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1998, the first writer in Portuguese to do so.
